questions.text: A software requirements specification (SRS) document should avoid discussing which one of the following?
questions.solution:
An SRS says what the system must do (functional and non-functional needs, interfaces, UI requirements). How it is built (the design) belongs in the design document.

Answer: Design specification

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Decision points: while, if, else if, and the final if = 4.

Cyclomatic complexity = 4 + 1 = 5

Answer: 5

Checking each statement:
- Condition coverage looks at the code: white-box (iii)
- Equivalence class partitioning uses only the specification: black-box (i)
- Volume testing checks behaviour under large data: performance (iv)
- Alpha testing is done on the whole system: system testing (ii)

Answer: P-iii, Q-i, R-iv, S-ii

questions.text: For a software project, the spiral model was employed. When will the spiral stop?
questions.solution:
The spiral model keeps looping through planning, risk analysis, engineering and evaluation for every new version. It ends only when the product is retired.

Answer: When the software product is retired

When the software product is released after Beta testing
When the risk analysis is completed

questions.text: The test suite (set of test input) used to perform unit testing on a module could cover 70% of the code. What is the reliability of the module if the probability of success is 0.95 during testing?
questions.solution:
Only 70% of the code is tested, and it passes with probability 0.95. Nothing is known about the untested 30%.

Reliability is at most 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.95 = 0.665.

Answer: At the most 0.665
